claims.author: l0rinc
claims.quote:
A few closely related cases seem worth covering as well:
- `-timeout` values above `INT_MAX` are narrowed before the new positivity check (similar ones were already attempted here and closed).
- Very large `-mempoolexpiry` values can overflow when converted from hours to seconds.
- A negative `-txconfirmtarget` wraps into the wallet's unsigned target and can make fee estimation fall back to `-fall
claims.request: Cover related configuration edge cases: -timeout above INT_MAX, -mempoolexpiry overflow from hours to seconds, negative -txconfirmtarget wrapping, and zero/negation handling for -limitclustersize and -bantime.

claims.author: l0rinc
claims.harm: The new test loop binds a std::string reference to temporary strings, causing CI to fail.
claims.quote: CI seems to fail because the new test loop binds a `std::string` reference to temporary strings.

claims.author: sedited
claims.harm: Argument validation should be handled centrally by the args handler itself rather than through piecemeal, bug-prone special cases (Approach NACK).
claims.quote: I think I'm Approach NACK at yet another piecemeal approach to a solution for this. This should be solved by the args handler itself, not with many different bug prone special cases.

claims.author: ryanofsky
claims.harm: DISALLOW_NEGATION is only a partial fix that allows invalid zero values to slip through if zero values cannot be accepted, because it only guards against them being set in one path.
claims.quote: If your option can't accept zero values, DISALLOW_NEGATION is only a partial fix and may allow zeroes to slip through because you are only guarding against them being set ib a single path. Better to check for valid values one place instead of multiple.

claims.author: ryanofsky
claims.harm: DISALLOW_NEGATION creates inconsistent user experience where -option=0 and -nooption behave differently without clear reason.
claims.quote: It creates inconsistent UX where -option=0 and -nooption have different behaviors without a clear reason, when normal behavior is for them to behave the same.

claims.author: ryanofsky
claims.harm: The PR substantially increases use of DISALLOW_NEGATION, a flag that was intended to be used rarely and eventually removed.
claims.quote: DISALLOW_NEGATION was intended to used rarely and eventually removed (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/22766#issuecomment-944924866) and this PR seems to increase usage by a lot.
